assessments.reasoning: The commit-pinned SPDX json/exceptions record has licenseExceptionId Autoconf-exception-generic, name “Autoconf generic exception” and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Its seeAlso list identifies Ubuntu xmltooling copyright, Debian sipwitch copyright, Apple launchd compile.auto and Gnulib’s gnulib-tool. The receipt identifies the generated JSON by SHA-256 f4cb47eedaf01a9d1342af1508ee9774eeedaf4786ea7b3b191991299a8ed0bc.

The GitHub API object for spdx/license-list-data identifies annotated tag 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as v3.29.0. Its target type is commit and its target SHA is 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in the generated JSON URL. The tag is unsigned. Authenticity rests on repository provenance.

The digest-matched Autoconf file provides the publisher-side text. Its “if you distribute this file” and “you may include it” clauses correspond to the displayed SPDX text. The separate preceding GPL grant supplies the specimen’s base edition.

challenge.method: I compared both generated exception entries with elisp-comp, checked SPDX’s Gnulib wording alternatives, and traced the annotated release tag to its target as required for a release-specific crosswalk under SCES §7.
challenge.results: The unsuffixed text ends with the file-inclusion permission, as elisp-comp does. The -3.0 entry adds a substantive sentence. The Gnulib template permits “this file may be distributed” and “under the same distribution terms as.” elisp-comp uses the displayed active wording, so the correspondence does not depend on those alternatives.

limitations: The comparison is documentary. Shell comment prefixes, wrapping and whitespace differ. No formal SPDX template match or byte equality is asserted.
SPDX’s listed examples are discovery leads. The record does not cite elisp-comp, and the linked witnesses were not independently inspected.
reasoning: At the target commit of v3.29.0, SPDX publishes Autoconf-exception-generic as a nondeprecated exception. Its text and elisp-comp agree on the file being distributed, the required generated script and the permission to use the rest of the program’s distribution terms.
